transcript:
00:00 - Lena Park: Okay thanks everyone for joining, we're gonna run through the Optimize quantization walkthrough focused on INT8 and FP8 and how that maps to quality vs latency. Hi Priya, Tom, Sofia.
00:06 - Priya Singh: Hi thanks, excited to see this. We're particularly concerned about hallucinations after quant and how it might hit our NPS.
00:12 - Ethan Chen: Totally understood. We'll show examples and tuned profiles; the goal is to give you the cost/latency tradeoff and the QA thresholds we use.
00:20 - Tom Baker: Quick infra context - we run inference on GCP A2s today, some experiments on A100s in a shared project, and we have a strict 150ms median token latency SLO for live chat.
00:32 - Lena Park: Great context that's helpful. We'll surface both throughput and per-token latency numbers. Note that INT8 typically gives ~1.8-2.5x lower memory and 20-40% latency reduction depending on kernels, FP8 can give better latency but sometimes is costlier on certain runtimes.
00:48 - Sofia Morales: Can you run the demo with one of our sample prompts? We sent over a small set earlier.
00:55 - Ethan Chen: Yep, I pulled a 10-message subset from the set Priya uploaded. I'll start with the baseline FP16 run on the model, then INT8, then FP8 profiles we have.
01:05 - (sound of keyboard)
01:12 - Ethan Chen: Baseline FP16 2-shot prompt, median token latency 145ms, 99th 310ms on the A100 dev node. Generation quality - coherence looks fine, no obvious regressions on this prompt.
01:26 - Priya Singh: That 145ms median is good, we need under 150ms but 99th of 310ms is concerning for spikes.
01:33 - Ethan Chen: Right, with INT8 profile applied we see median drop to 110ms, 99th to 230ms, approximate 25% median improvement. However we saw a slight token-level perplexity increase, and on a couple prompts a truncation/word choice difference that affected fidelity.
01:50 - Lena Park: Important nuance - INT8 is great for memory and latency but you need to validate across your test set; some edge-case factuality drops can appear. That's why our Optimize flow includes automated quality regressions checks.
02:06 - Tom Baker: How deterministic is FP8 across infra vendors? We have some experiments on TPUs as well.
02:13 - Ethan Chen: FP8 support varies; on NVIDIA Hopper/Grace we have optimized kernels that give consistent FP8 performance. On cloud TPUs or older Ampere nodes FP8 paths may not be as mature. For Atlas, A100/A4/cloud A100s are fine; we will include a compatibility note.
02:31 - Priya Singh: Can we quantify quality as accuracy or rouge? How did you measure the regressions?
02:38 - Ethan Chen: We run a mix: token-level perplexity, ROUGE-like n-gram overlap for generation tasks, and a human-eval subset for critical prompts. On the 10-sample run INT8 had a 1.5-2.2% relative drop on the ROUGE proxy, FP8 had ~0.6-1.0% drop but faster latency in some cases.
02:55 - Lena Park: Also our Optimize tool will run A/B on your prompt set and produce delta metrics, so you'll see exactly which prompts regress and by how much.
03:05 - Sofia Morales: For production, we're thinking of a canary where some percent of traffic uses INT8. How do fallbacks work?
03:12 - Ethan Chen: We support routing policies - canary traffic to quantized variant with automatic fallback to FP16 if quality thresholds are hit. We can route by percent or by latency buckets.
03:22 - Tom Baker: Any special monitoring for KV cache or long-context cases? We have 8k context windows.
03:29 - Ethan Chen: Yes, we monitor KV cache hit patterns and prefix reuse. Quantization sometimes affects numerical stability for very long sequences; our test suite includes 8k and 32k contexts depending on model. We'll run an 8k pass for your prompts in the pilot.
03:45 - Priya Singh: Security - will logs or tokens be stored differently when using Dedicated or Private? We need SOC2, SSO and KMS integration.
03:54 - Lena Park: Good question. For Dedicated and Private we can do customer-managed KMS, VPC-only control plane, and audit logs that meet SOC2 expectations. We'll attach our security pack and SOC2 report.
04:06 - (brief interruption)
04:12 - Ethan Chen: Back to quant: we'll show an example where INT8 introduced a hallucination on one prompt - not huge but enough to drop an evaluation metric. We then applied a mixed-precision fallback for the attention layers and the regression disappeared with a small latency cost.
04:28 - Priya Singh: Mixed precision fallback - is that automated or manual tuning?
04:33 - Ethan Chen: Optimize recommends a profile and will try selective layer fallbacks automatically in the tuning pass; you can also tune manually via our tuning guide. We'll share scripts to reproduce.
04:45 - Lena Park: For pricing, quantized instances reduce GPU footprint; we'll send an estimated cost-per-token delta in the spreadsheet. Typically INT8 reduces per-token cost by ~30-45% depending on batching and cache hit rates.
04:59 - Tom Baker: We need real numbers on our workload. Can you run a pilot on our dev cluster with our prompts?
05:05 - Lena Park: Yes, next step is pilot. We'll exchange test credentials and a small runner script from Ethan. He'll instrument latency, CPU/GPU utilization and quality diffs.
05:15 - Sofia Morales: Any vendor lock-in risks? If we start on Redwood Dedicated and later move to private on-prem, will profiles transfer?
05:22 - Ethan Chen: Profiles are portable; the profile is a set of config + kernel hints. Some kernel performance may vary by hardware, but model outputs and Selective fallback logic are consistent. We'll note any vendor-specific optimizations.
05:36 - Priya Singh: Competitor question - we've seen other platforms claim similar quant workflows. Why Redwood?
05:41 - Lena Park: Our differentiation is runtime-level kernels + Optimize's closed-loop evals so you don't just quantize once; you get continuous quality monitoring and automated fallbacks. Also unified API for hosted/dedicated/private.
05:54 - Tom Baker: Ok let's recap next steps.
06:00 - Lena Park: Recap: Lena sends quant benchmark spreadsheet + pricing; Ethan sends tuning guide and profiling script; Priya shares full prompt set and latency SLOs; we schedule pilot on Atlas dev cluster within two weeks.
06:13 - Priya Singh: Sounds good, we'll aim to have the prompt set over by Monday.
06:18 - Lena Park: Perfect. Any final questions?
06:22 - Sofia Morales: One small ask - can you include sample alert thresholds and dashboards we can plug into our Grafana?
06:28 - Ethan Chen: Yes we'll include JSON dashboards or a Grafana export.
06:33 - Lena Park: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
06:38 - (meeting ends)
